title: Load messages a page at a time
hints: Decide first which requests get the new response and which keep the old one. Write that branch in the route before anything else.
A page number or offset counts positions, and positions move when messages are added or deleted. What about a message never changes?
Make the cursor the id of the last message on the page, and return messages with a bigger id. Ask for one more than the limit to know if there's another page.

hiddenTestRules.paging > returns the first page and a cu: the result is { items, nextCursor }: up to limit messages, oldest first, and nextCursor is text you can pass back.
hiddenTestRules.paging > continues after the cursor: With a cursor, the page starts right after the last message of the page that cursor came from.
hiddenTestRules.paging > ends with a null cursor when th: nextCursor is null when there are no more messages, even when the last page is exactly full.
hiddenTestRules.paging > uses a limit of 20 when only a: A cursor with no limit uses a limit of 20.
hiddenTestRules.paging > rejects limits outside 1 to 100: A limit that isn't a whole number from 1 to 100 is 400 with { error: 'limit must be a whole number from 1 to 100' }.
hiddenTestRules.paging > rejects a limit with junk after: A limit that isn't a whole number from 1 to 100 is 400
hiddenTestRules.paging > rejects a cursor it never gave: A cursor that can't be read is 400 with { error: 'Invalid cursor' }.
hiddenTestRules.paging > skips nothing when an earlier m: Paging never skips or repeats a message when messages are added or deleted between pages.
hiddenTestRules.paging > still works when the cursor's o: This holds even if the message the cursor came from was deleted.
hiddenTestRules.paging > repeats nothing when a message: Paging never skips or repeats a message when messages are added or deleted between pages.
hiddenTestRules.paging > regression: the old list has no: With neither limit nor cursor, GET /messages stays exactly as it is today: a plain list of every message.
